nodes.label: Broker / trader systems
nodes.summary: Sends orders and receives execution reports. Orders are limit or market, buy or sell.

nodes.label: Order gateway
nodes.summary: Authenticates the session (FIX or a binary protocol), validates messages and checks sequence numbers. Retransmits missed messages on request.
nodes.details: FIX uses MsgSeqNum and ResendRequest for session recovery (checked in the earlier pass).

nodes.label: Pre-trade risk
nodes.summary: Checks limits, credit and wallet before an order may reach the book.

nodes.label: Sequencer + input disruptor
nodes.summary: Stamps every inbound event with a global sequence number. The input stage does unmarshalling, replication and journaling in parallel, since those tasks are independent.
nodes.details: LMAX: input disruptor, business logic processor, output disruptors. The Disruptor ring buffer follows a single-writer principle and reports 3 orders of magnitude lower mean latency and ~8× throughput versus queues.

nodes.label: Journal (event log)
nodes.summary: Durable log of sequenced inputs. State is rebuilt by replaying it, with snapshots to shorten recovery. A full restart including a day of journals took less than a minute at LMAX.

nodes.label: Matching engine (single thread)
nodes.summary: A deterministic state machine over the sequenced input: price-time priority, trades at the resting order's price. All state is in memory with no database. LMAX ran 6 million orders/s on one thread (2011 benchmark).
nodes.details: Sharded by symbol in the standard design, so each shard stays single-threaded.

nodes.label: Order book (in memory)
nodes.summary: Per symbol: bids and asks as price levels, each a FIFO list, plus a hash map from order ID to node for O(1) cancel. Best bid and ask are tracked.
nodes.details: Reading the best price is O(1). Finding the next level when one empties costs O(log P) or a tick scan (earlier pass).

nodes.label: Hot standby (replica)
nodes.summary: Runs the same deterministic engine on the same sequenced input. LMAX reports switching between processors in a matter of micro-seconds.

nodes.label: Market-data publisher
nodes.summary: Publishes trades and book updates with sequence numbers over UDP multicast so every subscriber sees the same stream. MoldUDP64 packets carry a session and the first message's sequence number.

nodes.label: Re-request server
nodes.summary: Answers unicast Request messages for missed packets. Snapshots come from a separate service (GLIMPSE in Nasdaq's case).
nodes.details: The GLIMPSE snapshot service was verified in the earlier pass.

nodes.label: Market-data subscribers
nodes.summary: Detects gaps from sequence numbers, requests retransmission, and rebuilds the book from the stream.

nodes.label: Matching core (one shard)
nodes.summary: The sequenced, single-threaded core: sequencer and input journaling, the deterministic engine and the in-memory order book.
nodes.details: Grouping container: it names the units the sources describe together. The components inside it are listed in the Components view.

steps.caption: A broker sends a limit order. The gateway checks the session and message sequence.
Pre-trade risk checks limits before the order can touch the book.
The sequencer gives the order the next global sequence number, which fixes fairness and ordering.
In parallel with replication and unmarshalling, the input is journaled so state can be rebuilt by replay.
The single-threaded deterministic engine processes events strictly in sequence.
It matches against the best opposite price while prices cross, trading at the resting order's price with FIFO at each level. Any remainder rests in the book.
Execution reports go back through the gateway.
The same events are published as market data.
Subscribers receive sequenced multicast packets. Each packet carries the sequence number of its first message.
A subscriber that sees a gap sends a Request for the missing packets to a re-request server, and gets them back by unicast.
A standby engine consumes the same sequenced input, so its state is identical.
After a restart, state is rebuilt by replaying the journal (with snapshots). LMAX reports full restarts in under a minute and processor switchover in micro-seconds.
